itineraryStops[1].name: Seongsan Ilchulbong
itineraryStops[1].category: UNESCO Tuff Cone — Sunrise Peak (Triple UNESCO Designation)
itineraryStops[1].description: **Seongsan Ilchulbong (성산일출봉, 'Sunrise Peak')** is a **5,000-year-old Surtseyan-type hydrovolcanic tuff cone** — a rare landform created when an underwater basalt eruption broke the sea surface, the magma met seawater, and the resulting steam-explosive ash built a **182 m fortress-shaped crater** rim instead of a typical lava cone. The result is what UNESCO formally calls **'an exceptional example of an emergent Surtseyan-type volcanic edifice'**. The crater is **600 m wide × 90 m deep**, ringed by **99 jagged rim rocks** that local lore likens to a stone crown. Seongsan carries the **Triple UNESCO designation**: **World Natural Heritage (inscribed 2007-07-02)** as part of the **'Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes' property**, **Biosphere Reserve (2002)**, and **Global Geopark (2010-10)** — a stack matched only by Hallasan itself among Korean sites. **18 Imperial Japanese WWII caves** (kamikaze suicide-boat shelters, 1945) are tunneled into the seaward base. Trail: **0.8 km one-way, ~140 m elevation gain, 60 min round trip** on wide stone steps. **Haenyeo (해녀) demonstrations** run **daily at 13:30 and 15:00** at the rocky cove below the cone — Jeju women divers (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage 2016) descend without scuba gear. Admission updated **April 2025**: **Adult ₩5,000 / Youth+Child ₩2,500 / Group adult ₩1,600**, free under 7 and over 65. The summit deck is also part of the **Yeongjusipgyeong (Jeju 10 Scenic Wonders) canon**, and remains Korea's premier **annual New Year sunrise pilgrimage** destination — 50,000+ visitors ascend before dawn on January 1, with municipal sunrise-festival programming since 1995. **Udo Island (우도, 'Cow Island')** — Korea's largest secondary volcanic island — is clearly visible 4 km offshore from the summit, accessible by **15-min ferry from Seongsan Port** (₩10,500 round-trip) for guests with extra time on a different itinerary.

itineraryStops[2].name: Seopjikoji (East Cape)
itineraryStops[2].category: Volcanic Cape — Tadao Ando Architecture + Bangdupo Lighthouse + Drama Filming
itineraryStops[2].description: **Seopjikoji (섭지코지)** is a narrow volcanic cape on Jeju's east coast — the name compounds **'Seopji' (narrow piece of land) + 'Koji' (Jeju dialect for 'cape')**. The **2.1 km cliff-edge trail (~30 min, only 14 m elevation gain)** is one of the island's most photographed coastal walks, anchored by three cultural-architectural moments. **(1) Bulgeun Oreum (붉은 오름)** — a red-tinged volcanic parasitic cone at the cape's tip, capped by the **octagonal Bangdupo Lighthouse (방두포 등대)** which **flashes every 4 seconds** and remains in operation as a coastal navigation aid. **(2) The Hyeopja Yeondae Beacon Fire Station (협자연대)** — a **4 m tall × 9 m diameter Joseon-era smoke-signal mound built of volcanic stone**, designated **Special Monument No. 23-2** by Jeju Province — one of 38 such yeondae beacons that ringed the island as a 16th–18th-century early-warning system against pirate raids. **(3) Tadao Ando architecture** — Pulitzer-laureate Japanese architect **Tadao Ando (안도 다다오)** designed two buildings on site: the **Glass House (글라스 하우스)** restaurant and the **Yumin Art Gallery (유민 미술관)**, both characteristic of Ando's signature concrete-and-light minimalism, completed for the Phoenix Island resort development. Offshore, the **10 m volcanic neck Seonbawi (선바위, 'Seon Rock')** is featured in local **dragon king's youngest son** legend. Drama-filming credits include **'All In' (2003, SBS), 'My Girl' (2005, SBS), 'Legend of Gingko', 'The Uprising', and 'Cheonilya'**. **Spring canola fields** flood the slopes **March–April (yellow)**; **summer hydrangea blooms** follow in **June (blue/violet)**. **FREE admission** to the cape; Yumin Art Gallery and Glass House restaurant separately ticketed/reserved.

itineraryStops[4].name: Seongeup Folk Village
itineraryStops[4].category: Joseon-era Walled Town — Important Folklore Cultural Heritage (1423 founding)
itineraryStops[4].description: **Seongeup Folk Village (성읍 민속마을)** is a **living Joseon-era walled town founded in 1423** during the reign of **Sejong the Great** as Jeong-eui-hyeon (정의현), one of the three administrative seats of Joseon-era Jeju. The village served continuously as a **county administrative center until 1914** — nearly **500 years** — and retains **110 traditional structures** today within the original eupseong (읍성) walled-town footprint, designed on **Korean feng shui principles** typical of Joseon county capitals. The entire village is designated **Important Folklore Cultural Heritage of South Korea**, with **multiple individual buildings** carrying separate heritage status. At the village center stand **two ancient trees designated Natural Monuments of South Korea** — a **Saw-leaf Zelkova (느티나무)** and a **Japanese Hackberry (팽나무)**, both estimated **600+ years old** and revered as the village's spiritual anchor. Historical scars are visible: a **major fire in 1826 destroyed ~80 buildings**, and the village suffered fire damage **during the Jeju Uprising in 1948** — both events preserved as historical record on village signage. The **peak household count (historical, pre-modern) was ~1,500** — today the village remains inhabited by ~250 families, many actively maintaining traditional crafts. Drama filming credit: **'Dae Jang Geum (Jewel in the Palace)' (MBC, 2003–2004)**, the international K-drama hit. Local specialty: **Omegisul (오메기술)** — a **rice-based traditional Jeju liquor** brewed by **one family for multiple generations**, with the brewing demonstrated and tasted free of charge at the home-brewery within the village. **FREE admission**; outdoor walking dominates (~70% outdoor / 30% indoor for individual hanok visits).

itineraryStops[5].description: Return drive to the **Jeju International Passenger Terminal** (제주항 국제여객터미널) on Jeju City's northern coast. The route from East Jeju (Seongsan/Seongeup area) takes ~70–80 minutes via Highway 1132 (the coastal ring road) and Route 16, with one designated comfort stop. Drop-off is timed to deliver guests to the terminal **at least 60 minutes before your ship's all-aboard time**, matching the cruise industry's standard buffer for embarkation queues. The vehicle pulls into the **100-bus parking capacity lot**, guests disembark at the terminal entrance with luggage assistance from the driver/guide. If guests have early evening flights from Jeju International Airport, **Bus #100 connects directly from the cruise terminal to the airport** — the guide can advise on this option. The terminal interior offers convenience store, pharmacy, snack shop, souvenir shops with **tax-free items**, Jeju Bank ATM accepting overseas cards, currency exchange (typical hours 08:00–17:00), and SK Telecom T-mobile Wi-Fi rental counter — useful if guests want last-minute purchases or to reload mobile data before sailaway. **Free shuttle bus to Dongmun Traditional Market** (oldest/largest in Jeju City, ~10 min) is also available for any guests with extra time before all-aboard.

Admission: **Adult ₩2,000 / Youth ₩1,000 / FREE under 7 and over 65**. Lunch duration is **~60 minutes**, fitting the cruise day-trip timeline. Beverages: barley tea (free), **Jeju Beer** (~₩6,000), **Hallasan Soju** (~₩5,000), or **Omegisul rice-millet liquor** (Seongeup family recipe — sold at the market's licensed vendors). All venues in the rotation accept **major cards + cash KRW**; bilingual photo menus (English/Chinese) standard. Lunch is **NOT included** in cruise tour pricing — typical out-of-pocket **₩15,000–25,000/pax**; inclusive lunch upgrade available on booking. After lunch, the natural flow is **5-min walk → Cheonjiyeon Falls trailhead → 1 km gentle gorge walk** — making this particularly most efficient lunch-to-attraction transition for cruise day-trips.

The guide stays with the group through the meal, advising on galchi sashimi vs grilled galchi, recommending which black-pork stall has the day's freshest cut, and translating the family-run vendors who don't speak English. **5-min walk to Cheonjiyeon Falls trailhead** afterward — the small-group format makes this market-to-falls transition feel like an unhurried stroll, not a tour-leader-counted manifest move.
itinerary_variants[1].stops[4].name: Cheonjiyeon Falls (Seogwipo old-town waterfall)
itinerary_variants[1].stops[4].descripti: **Cheonjiyeon Falls** (천지연 폭포 — literally 'Sky-meeting-Land Falls') is the closer-to-port of Seogwipo's two famous waterfalls and is **NOT to be confused with Cheonjeyeon Falls** (천제연 — the three-tier 'Pond of the Heavenly Emperor' falls in Jungmun, ~15 min west). The single-tier cascade plunges **22 m / 12 m wide into a 20 m-deep emerald pool** at the end of a **gentle 1 km riverside trail** (~15 min one-way, paved and stroller-friendly) that follows a subtropical gorge dense with **rare plants**: **Damselfly Tree** (Natural Monument No. 163), **Crepidomanes makinoi** ferns clinging to the basalt walls, and dozens of endemic species protected as **Natural Monument No. 379** (the falls + surrounding habitat ensemble). The pool below is the protected habitat of the **Mutae eel** (마부태 / 무태 — *Anguilla marmorata*, the marbled eel), itself **Natural Monument No. 27** — a nocturnal species whose movement under nighttime illumination is one of Cheonjiyeon's signature scenes. Admission is **₩2,000 adults / ₩1,000 children** (one of Jeju's most affordable nature stops); operating hours **09:00–22:00 (last entry 21:30)** — the **after-dark illumination program 19:00–22:00** is unique among Jeju waterfalls and turns the gorge walls + falls into an emerald-jade light show, often paired with cruise overnight stays. The trailhead is **a 5-minute walk from Olle Maeil Market**, making the two stops a natural pairing on cruise day-trips originating from Gangjeong port. On clear days, **Munseom Island** (3 km offshore — Korea's first marine-park designation, 1994) is visible from the falls observation deck, and the basalt cliff faces of the gorge expose the same Hallasan-flank lava-flow stratigraphy as Daepo Jusangjeolli.

itinerary_variants[1].stops[5].name: Olle Maeil Market (Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market)
itinerary_variants[1].stops[5].descripti: **Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market** (서귀포 매일올레시장) is **South Jeju's largest traditional market** and the closest food-and-shopping anchor to Gangjeong cruise port (~10 min drive). Established in **the early 1960s**, the market today runs a **620 m covered arcade with ~200 shops and ~140 vendors**, all under a translucent retractable roof that keeps shoppers dry in Jeju's frequent showers. The **'Maeil Olle'** name combines *Maeil* ('every day' — open daily, no fixed closure) with *Olle* (Jeju's famous walking-trail network — Trail Course 6 passes near the market entrance, and Course 7 connects southward to Cheonjiyeon Falls and the Seogwipo waterfront). Signature foods to look for: **Jeseong Bakery's octopus buns** (locally famous, queues form by 10:00); **hallabong + cheonhyehyang citrus** in winter (December–March, the famous Jeju mandarin hybrids); **fresh hairtail (galchi) sashimi**; **black pork skewers**; **Mom-guk** (traditional Jeju seaweed soup); and **Omegisul** (the rice-millet liquor brewed in Seongeup — sold here in tasting bottles). Hours are roughly **07:00–21:00** (vendor-by-vendor variable), and most of the older vendors accept cash only — though tax-refund and card-accepting modern stalls have multiplied since 2018. The market is a **5-minute walk from Cheonjiyeon Falls trailhead**, making Cheonjiyeon + Olle a natural lunch-and-stroll pairing — guides typically schedule lunch (Jeju seafood or black-pork) at one of the market's sit-down stalls before the falls visit, taking advantage of the food density before walking off the meal at the gorge.

itinerary_variants[1].stops[6].name: Return to Gangjeong Cruise Terminal (Seogwipo — south)
itinerary_variants[1].stops[6].descripti: Return drive to the **Gangjeong Port Cruise Terminal** in Seogwipo's Gangjeong Village. From the southern circuit (Olle Maeil Market / Cheonjiyeon Falls / downtown Seogwipo area) the drive is short — **~10–15 min via local roads**. From Hallasan 1100 Highland the descent takes ~35 min via Route 1100 (the same highest-altitude national highway you ascended in the morning). Drop-off is timed to deliver guests **at least 60 minutes before your ship's all-aboard time**, matching cruise industry standard buffers. The vehicle pulls into the **53-bus outdoor parking area**, guests disembark at the terminal entrance with luggage assistance from the driver/guide. Inside the terminal: tourist information center (multilingual), convenience store, currency exchange, lounge, tax-refund counter. If guests dock at Gangjeong with same-day evening flights, **Limousine Bus 800 / 800-1** connects from Gangjeong-area to Jeju International Airport via Seogwipo Innovation City (driver must be informed of destination before tap-in). The southern itinerary keeps stops within **30-min radius of the port** — the comfortable 8-hour window is built around this geography. **Note**: Anti-base activists hold daily Catholic mass + 100-bow protests at the main gate (separate from cruise-passenger areas, away from the terminal — cruise guests rarely encounter these activities on the standard arrival/departure path).

staticQuestions[0].question: How do I know which port my cruise calls at?
staticQuestions[0].answer: Your cruise booking confirmation lists the Jeju port. We confirm the port with you at booking and route the day accordingly. Most major cruise lines call at Jeju Port (north terminal); some Seogwipo-area calls use Gangjeong Port.
staticQuestions[1].question: Will I be back to the ship in time?
staticQuestions[1].answer: Yes. Both variants return to the cruise terminal between 16:30-17:00, with buffer for any traffic delay. We track your sailaway time and adjust pace if conditions change.
staticQuestions[2].question: What if my cruise call port changes?
staticQuestions[2].answer: Notify us as soon as you know — we switch the route variant to match. Port-routing is the whole reason this tour has two variants instead of one.
